title: Shared profile
description: data/_profile.yml — values common to every document, merged underneath each resume and cover letter beside it. The document always wins; this file only fills in what a document leaves out. Delete the file to turn the whole mechanism off.

name.description: Your name, split in two because the design styles them differently — the last name is set bolder than the first.

first.description: Given name, shown in the lighter weight.

contact.description: Contact details. Change a number here and it changes on every resume and every cover letter — that is the point of this file.

address.description: Shown on its own line. Usually just 'City, State'.

rows.description: Clickable contact lines. A document that sets contact.rows replaces this whole list rather than adding to it.

href.description: What clicking it does: 'tel:', 'mailto:', 'https:' or 'http:', written in full. Empty means no link.

role.description: A fallback subtitle under your name. Rarely useful here — 'role' names the job you are applying for, so it almost always belongs in the document instead. Kept available for a standing title you never change.

meta.description: 'lang' and 'maxPages' belong here — both are standing decisions rather than per-application ones. 'description' names the target role, so it stays in each document.

lang.description: BCP 47 language tag, stamped into the PDF so screen readers pronounce it correctly. Anything that is not a tag is marked en-US, with a warning.

description.description: A fallback metadata sentence for a document that sets none. Prefer writing a specific one per application — this sentence names the target role and is read by some applicant tracking systems.

maxPages.description: The ceiling the layout solver works under, for every resume. A document that needs more room sets its own maxPages, which wins. The cover letter has no solver and ignores this.
